26-qf2-qb-1308.solution: The interquartile range is Q3 − Q1. Here that is 35 − 15 = 20.
26-qf2-qb-1308.trick: Subtract in your head: 35 − 15 = 20. No halving and no median needed.

26-qf2-qb-1313.solution: Each whole step of magnitude multiplies the energy by 10 to the power 1.5, which is about 32. The gap is 7.0 − 5.0 = 2 steps, so the ratio is 10 to the power (1.5 × 2) = 10³. By shaking amplitude it would be 10² = 100 instead, but the show's 1,000 follows the energy reading. So the answer is 1,000.
26-qf2-qb-1313.trick: Each magnitude step is about 32 times the energy, so two steps give 32 × 32 ≈ 1,000. Amplitude would give 10 × 10 = 100, but the show took the energy answer.
26-qf2-qb-1313.comment: The word intensity is ambiguous. Two magnitude steps give 10² = 100 times the shaking amplitude but 10³ = 1,000 times the energy released, so the show's 1,000 only fits the energy reading.

26-qf2-qb-1317.solution: K means thousand, so add 50K + 30K + 20K = 100K. That is ₦100,000.
26-qf2-qb-1317.trick: Add the plain numbers, 50 + 30 + 20 = 100, then put the K back: ₦100,000.

26-qf2-qb-1320.solution: Each change multiplies the price: 1.10 × 0.95 × 1.08. First 1.10 × 0.95 = 1.045, then 1.045 × 1.08 = 1.1286. That is a net rise of 12.86%, which is about 13%.
26-qf2-qb-1320.trick: Small changes roughly add: 10 − 5 + 8 = 13. The options are far apart, so 13% is clearly the closest to the exact 12.86%.

26-qf2-qb-1329.solution: The correlation coefficient r runs from −1, a perfect opposite link, to 1, a perfect matching link. No linear link at all sits in the middle. So uncorrelated variables have r = 0.
26-qf2-qb-1329.trick: 1 and −1 are perfect relationships, so uncorrelated cannot be either of them. It is the middle of the scale: 0.

26-qf2-qb-1333.solution: The ratio 1 : 2 : 4 has 1 + 2 + 4 = 7 parts. One part is 35 ÷ 7 = 5 kg. Sand is 2 parts, so 2 × 5 = 10 kg.
26-qf2-qb-1333.trick: 35 is 7 × 5, so one part is 5 kg. Sand is 2 parts, which is 10 kg.

26-qf2-qb-1341.solution: Assume the data are roughly normal. 60 and 80 are 70 − 10 and 70 + 10, so they sit exactly 1 SD below and above the mean. About 68% of values lie within 1 SD of the mean (68.27% to be exact). So the answer is 68%.
26-qf2-qb-1341.trick: 60 and 80 are the mean ± 10, which is exactly 1 SD each side. The 68, 95, 99.7 rule gives 68%.

26-qf2-qb-1391.solution: Remove the lowest value, 12. The rest are 16, 18, 22 and 24, which add up to 80. The mean is 80 ÷ 4 = 20.
26-qf2-qb-1391.trick: The four left over pair up: 16 + 24 = 40 and 18 + 22 = 40. They balance around 20, so the mean is 20.

26-qf2-qb-1405.solution: The mean is below the mode, so the skewness is negative. Pearson's first coefficient of skewness is (mean − mode) ÷ SD = (50 − 55) ÷ 5 = −5 ÷ 5 = −1.
26-qf2-qb-1405.trick: The mean is 5 below the mode, and 5 is exactly 1 SD, so the size is 1. Mean below mode makes it negative: −1.

26-qf2-qb-1407.solution: Percentage increase = (new − old) ÷ old × 100. That is (120 − 80) ÷ 80 × 100 = 40 ÷ 80 × 100 = 50%.
26-qf2-qb-1407.trick: The rise of 40 is half of the starting 80, so it is 50%.

26-qf2-qb-1417.solution: The peak is where the velocity is zero. dh/dt = −32t + 64 = 0 gives t = 64 ÷ 32 = 2. So the maximum height is reached after 2 seconds.
26-qf2-qb-1417.trick: Peak of a parabola: t = −b ÷ (2a) = −64 ÷ (−32) = 2. It is also halfway between the zeros at t = 0 and t = 4.

26-qf2-qb-1460.solution: The amount of solute stays the same. It is 0.2 L × 5 M = 1 mol. The new volume is 200 + 800 = 1,000 mL = 1 L, so the molarity is 1 mol ÷ 1 L = 1 M.
26-qf2-qb-1460.trick: The volume grows from 200 mL to 1,000 mL, which is 5 times bigger, so the 5 M falls to a fifth: 1 M.

26-qf2-qb-1464.solution: Use the dot product: A·B = |A||B| cos θ. A·B = 3 × 4 + 4 × (−3) = 12 − 12 = 0. So cos θ = 0 and θ = 90°.
26-qf2-qb-1464.trick: Multiply across and add: 3 × 4 = 12 and 4 × (−3) = −12 cancel to 0. A zero dot product means the vectors are at right angles.

26-qf2-qb-1468.solution: Convert the speed: 90 km/h ÷ 3.6 = 25 m/s. Slowing to a stop in 5 s means a = 25 ÷ 5 = 5 m/s². The braking force is F = ma = 1,500 × 5 = 7,500 N.
26-qf2-qb-1468.trick: 90 km/h is 25 m/s (divide by 3.6). Losing 25 m/s in 5 s is 5 m/s², and 1,500 × 5 = 7,500.

26-qf2-qb-1476.solution: Differentiate twice. f(x) = x³ gives f′(x) = 3x², then f″(x) = 6x. At x = 2, f″(2) = 6 × 2 = 12.
26-qf2-qb-1476.trick: Bring the power down and lower it by one, twice: x³ to 3x² to 6x. Then 6 × 2 = 12.

26-qf2-qb-1487.solution: Time = pages ÷ pages per minute. That is 300 ÷ 12 = 25 minutes.
26-qf2-qb-1487.trick: Divide top and bottom by 3: 300 ÷ 12 is 100 ÷ 4, which is 25.

26-qf2-qb-1495.solution: Differentiate twice. y = x³ + 2x² gives y′ = 3x² + 4x, then y″ = 6x + 4. At x = 1, y″ = 6 + 4 = 10.
26-qf2-qb-1495.trick: Take the second derivative term by term: x³ gives 6x and 2x² gives 4. At x = 1 that is 6 + 4 = 10.

26-qf2-qb-1508.solution: Complete the square: x² − 2x + 5 = (x − 1)² + 4. A square is never negative, so the smallest value is 4, reached at x = 1.
26-qf2-qb-1508.trick: The lowest point is at x = 2 ÷ 2 = 1. Put in 1: 1 − 2 + 5 = 4.

26-qf2-qb-1522.solution: The amount of HCl stays the same, so M₁V₁ = M₂V₂. In litres, 3 × 0.9 = M₂ × 3, so M₂ = 2.7 ÷ 3 = 0.9 M.
26-qf2-qb-1522.trick: M₂ = 3 × 0.9 ÷ 3. The two 3s cancel, which leaves 0.9.

26-qf2-qb-1543.solution: With the mean and median given, use Pearson's second coefficient: skewness = 3 × (mean − median) ÷ SD. So 1.5 = 3 × (72 − 68) ÷ SD = 12 ÷ SD. Then SD = 12 ÷ 1.5 = 8.

26-qf2-qb-1548.solution: Covariance = correlation × SD₁ × SD₂. That is 0.75 × 6 × 12 = 0.75 × 72 = 54.

26-qf2-qb-1557.solution: A 1 : 10 model means every length is 10 times bigger on the real bridge. Strength follows cross section area, which grows 10² = 100 times, so 5 kg × 100 = 500 kg. Scaling by volume, 10³ = 1,000 times, gives 5,000 kg, which is 5 tonnes. The show accepted both: 500 kg or 5 tonnes.
26-qf2-qb-1557.trick: Multiply 5 kg by 100 (10 × 10, for area) to get 500 kg, or by 1,000 (10 × 10 × 10, for volume) to get 5 tonnes. Either was accepted.
26-qf2-qb-1557.computed: 500 kg by area scaling (5 tonnes by volume scaling)
26-qf2-qb-1557.comment: The question does not say how load capacity scales. By cross section area it is 10² = 100 times (500 kg), and by volume it is 10³ = 1,000 times (5,000 kg or 5 tonnes). The show accepted both, so both are kept.

26-qf2-qb-1567.solution: The perimeter is 200 m, so length + width = 100 m. The area l × (100 − l) is largest when l = 50, which also makes the width 50. So the best shape is a square, 50 m × 50 m, with area 2,500 m².
26-qf2-qb-1567.trick: Check the fence each option uses: 4 × 30 = 120 m and 4 × 20 = 80 m leave fence unused, while 4 × 50 = 200 m uses it all. A square is the best rectangle for a fixed perimeter.

26-qf2-qb-1600.solution: Midrange = (minimum + maximum) ÷ 2. So 30 = (10 + max) ÷ 2, which gives 10 + max = 60. The maximum is 50.
26-qf2-qb-1600.trick: The midrange 30 is 20 above the minimum 10, so the maximum is 20 above 30: 50.

26-qf2-qb-1606.solution: Elastic energy = ½kx². That is ½ × 600 × (0.1)² = 300 × 0.01 = 3 J.
